content.value_statement: Recent code changes can drift from project style and become harder to maintain. This skill refines touched code for clarity, consistency, and behavior preservation.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recently modified code for readability and maintainability issues.
Applies project-specific standards from CLAUDE.md when available.
Prefers explicit, readable structure over compact or clever code.
Reduces unnecessary nesting, redundant logic, and unclear naming.
Preserves existing behavior while improving code organization.
limitations: It focuses on recently touched code unless asked to review more.
It depends on available project standards and surrounding context.
It does not replace tests for proving behavior is unchanged.
It may skip useful abstractions that require domain knowledge.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Feature Work
use_cases.description: Refine a new feature after implementation so the final code is easier to review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Improve naming, structure, and style before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Enforce Local Style
use_cases.description: Apply team conventions from project documentation during routine coding sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify My Recent Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill on my recently modified files. Preserve behavior and focus on readability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after finishing a small change

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the touched code against our project standards. Refine naming, imports, types, and component structure.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Complexity
prompt_templates.prompt: Simplify the recent changes by reducing nesting and redundant logic. Keep explicit control flow where it improves clarity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Moderate refactor after adding conditional logic

prompt_templates.title: Audit Refactor Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine the modified code and explain any material cleanup choices. Avoid changes that could alter behavior or remove useful abstractions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for sensitive code paths

output_examples.input: I changed a React settings panel and want it cleaned up before review.
output_examples.output: The skill would simplify component structure, clarify prop types, sort imports, and keep the visible behavior unchanged.

output_examples.input: I added validation logic with several nested conditions.
output_examples.output: The skill would replace hard-to-read nesting with explicit branches and clearer names while preserving validation outcomes.

output_examples.input: I updated a utility module and want it aligned with local style.
output_examples.output: The skill would apply local naming, module, and return type conventions from the project documentation.

best_practices: Use it after each meaningful coding session, before opening a review.
Keep tests nearby so behavior preservation can be checked.
Provide project style documents when local conventions matter.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to rewrite unrelated files without a clear scope.
Do not ask it to minimize line count at the cost of clarity.
Do not treat cleanup as a substitute for tests or review.

faq.question: What does this skill improve?
faq.answer: It improves readability, consistency, naming, structure, and maintainability in recently modified code.

faq.question: Does it change application behavior?
faq.answer: The skill is designed to preserve behavior. Tests are still recommended for important changes.

faq.question: Which files does it review?
faq.answer: It focuses on code touched in the current session unless you request a wider review.

faq.question: Can it follow team coding standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses available project guidance, including CLAUDE.md when the file exists.

faq.question: Is this a full refactoring tool?
faq.answer: No. It performs focused cleanup and simplification, not broad architecture redesign.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
